prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single transparent pixel-art character sprite for The Daily Meili office app.
Create a small owl coworker based on the user's original owl drawings, matching the visual language of Pip's existing pixel corgi sprites.
Input image 1 (IMG_0770.jpg): primary owl identity and colors, not a scene to reproduce. Preserve the compact upright rounded-square body, two short horn-like feather tufts, pale cool-gray feathers, large white connected facial mask, white oval belly, tiny dark beak, short charcoal feet, and distinctive red neckerchief.
Input image 2 (IMG_3793.png): secondary identity/proportion reference only; ignore the text and objects in this sketch.
Input image 3 (pip-atlas.png): style reference ONLY: match its chunky clean stepped pixel outlines, simple face, restrained palette and friendly small office-worker proportions. Do not include or transform the corgi.
Add neatly fitted round dark-rimmed glasses with a small bridge, two simple dark pupils inside clear lenses. Keep the face extremely readable: glasses are the sole dark eye rims, no doubled eye circles, no uncanny eyes, no elaborate highlights. Tiny beak below the bridge. Expression quietly curious and pleased. Slight three-quarter view facing screen-right, both eyes visible. Both short wings resting naturally against body, exactly two wings and two feet. Feather tufts short and owlish, not tall dog ears. Full body standing idle, centered with generous clear padding, one character only.
Palette: near-black warm-charcoal outline; slate-gray and light gray feather planes; warm white face and belly; muted vermilion red scarf with two short ends. Approximately 8 flat colors, maximum 2 shade steps per material. Crisp deliberate pixel clusters, chunky 1-2 source-pixel outlines, visual resolution about a 96-pixel-tall game sprite enlarged with nearest-neighbor edges. No gradients, soft airbrushing, antialias blur, painterly texture, or 3D lighting. Cute and capable rather than babyish. No text, letters, slogans, labels, watermark, desk, chalkboard, floor, scene, badge or extra accessories. Background must be genuinely transparent, with no checkerboard painted in. Output one polished standalone sprite, not a contact sheet.
